newsitem.title: USA: US officials optimistic on Russian oil legislation.
newsitem.headline: US officials optimistic on Russian oil legislation.

text.p: U.S. officials said Friday they were optimistic that the Russian parliament would pass legislation setting out more favorable terms for oil and gas production-sharing agreements and listing properties that would be open to foreign investors.
Over the last four years, U.S. and Russian energy officials have discussed the need for energy laws that would encourage foreign investment.
An oil law signed last year came under heavy criticism from oil majors after it was revised to quell concerns among Russian conservatives that Moscow was giving away resources.
Following talks with Russian energy officials this week, Associate Deputy Energy Secretary Kyle Simpson said the tone of conversations had changed.

He said the main question surrounding the "law on the lists" was how many properties should be open to foreign investors. "They expressed a desire to get (production sharing and properties list) laws passed and spoke in terms of months for those two things," Simpson said.
"It seems to me the question of whether these laws need to be passed and changed has been crossed," he said in a telephone news conference. "Now it's a matter of when."

"A sound, transparent legal framework ... is essential to (investors) to verify their risk and gains, so they may make prudent judgments," Acting U.S. Energy Secretary Charles Curtis said at a luncheon for the Moscow International Petroleum Club.

The club's meeting here coincided with a meeting of an economic commission headed by U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, which included talks among energy officials.
The Russians specifically mentioned three oil joint ventures that they were eager to see signed, Simpson said, naming Northern Territories, Timan Pechora, and Priobskoye.
The Timan Pechora consortium groups Texaco Inc, Exxon Corp, Amoco Corp, and Norsk Hydro A/S of Norway.
The Priobskoye venture involves Amoco Corp.
The Northern Territories venture involves Conoco, a subsidiary of DuPont Co.
